function.mechanism: Hydrophilic alginate polymer increases viscosity and water retention; in suitable conditions it contributes to gel network formation and emulsion stabilization.
common_food_categories: Other foods at low residual levels

adi.basis: No numerical ADI needed (equivalent to ADI not specified) in EFSA 2017 re-evaluation of E400-E404.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses, but noted insufficient data for certain infant/young-child FSMP categories and advised exposure to remain below therapeutic-dose ranges where GI side effects occur.

adi.basis: ADI not specified (group ADI for alginic acid and ammonium/calcium/potassium/sodium salts).

concerns.summary: High intakes are associated with gastrointestinal/laxative effects; EFSA flagged infant/young-child FSMP contexts as insufficiently characterized for safety.
EFSA highlighted potential hypersensitivity relevance of residual protein impurities and recommended reducing protein limits in specifications.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA concluded no concern for genotoxicity for alginic acid and its salts (E400-E404).
EFSA did not identify carcinogenic concern from available long-term animal evidence.
JECFA allocated ADI not specified to alginic acid salts group.

populations: Infants (12 weeks-11 months) at higher dietary exposure estimates
Toddlers/young children consuming FSMP categories 13.1.5.1 and 13.1.5.2
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI exists; concern is context-specific (infant/young-child medical-diet categories with limited dedicated safety data and proximity to therapeutic-dose GI side-effect ranges).

risk_assessment.rationale: Core regulatory evaluations support broad safety at approved uses, but EFSA retained a meaningful caveat for specific infant/young-child FSMP uses and acknowledged GI effects at higher intakes.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI required and no general safety concern at refined reported-use exposure
EFSA 2017: inadequate data for certain infant/young-child FSMP categories
JECFA: ADI not specified with high-intake laxative caveat
US: affirmed GRAS with explicit use limits in 21 CFR 184.1610
